$comment: Scoped permissions so ingestion can run unattended -- both a headless
which otherwise stalls on its first Bash call with nobody there to approve.
The allow-list is deliberately per-script rather than a blanket
Bash(python3 scripts/*), so adding a new script is a conscious decision
rather than something that inherits unattended execution for free.
The deny rules encode CLAUDE.md's hard invariants. deny wins over allow, so
these hold even if an allow rule is later loosened:
- git is forbidden to agents; only the orchestrator commits
- raw/ transcript CONTENTS are immutable (mv between the two raw trees is
the one permitted change, and is allowed below)
- no deletion: transcripts are expensive to re-transcribe
- no network: every fact must come from the transcript on disk
File rules use Edit(path) only. A Write(path) rule is inert -- Edit(path)
is what covers every file-editing tool, Write included.
